name: MO-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans about nineteen points Republican in an open seat
Stigall holds a roughly 8-to-1 fundraising edge over Smead
Prediction markets price the Democrat at about four percent
A Democratic-favorable national environment only partially offsets the lean
model.rationale: Sam Graves's retirement does not change the underlying math in a district that leans nearly twenty points Republican, and Chris Stigall's large money advantage plus market pricing near four percent for the Democrat leave little case for an upset. A favorable environment trims the expected margin slightly but keeps the seat safely Republican.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected misstep by Stigall could narrow the margin, though not likely enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Sam Graves (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Northwest Missouri's sixth district is among the most Republican-leaning seats on this year's ballot, with a partisan lean of roughly nineteen points to the right. Sam Graves's retirement leaves the seat open, but Republican Chris Stigall starts with a large financial advantage, having raised about $599,000 to Democrat Josh Smead's $72,000. Outside groups have spent modestly against Stigall and nothing measurable for Smead, while a Libertarian candidate adds minor uncertainty.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a four percent chance of winning. A favorable national environment for Democrats trims the expected margin somewhat, but not nearly enough to put the seat in play. The forecast expects Stigall to win by a wide, though not overwhelming, margin.
